mission: 'A set of researchers doing empirical work with language models that aims to address longer-term concerns about the impacts of deploying highly-capable AI systems.' Founded by Sam Bowman, it overlaps with NYU's ML² , CILVR, the Center for Data Science and Linguistics. Its website has seen few new posts since 2023; Bowman now works on alignment at Anthropic. Founding year approximate (from the group's introductory post).

key_work.title: Eight Things to Know about Large Language Models
key_work.plain_summary: Bowman's short survey: LLMs get predictably more capable with scale but specific skills emerge unpredictably, experts can't reliably interpret them, and steering them is unreliable.

key_work.title: Why I Think More NLP Researchers Should Engage with AI Safety Concerns
key_work.plain_summary: A blog post arguing NLP researchers are well placed to work on risks from highly capable language models.

key_work.title: Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models
key_work.plain_summary: Proposed an experimental setup where non-experts assisted by an AI try to answer questions they couldn't answer alone, as a way to test oversight methods.

key_work.title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
key_work.plain_summary: Very hard expert-written questions designed for scalable-oversight research, where even skilled non-experts with web access do poorly.

people.role: Founder (associate professor, NYU; now at Anthropic)

warnings.text: Steering and controlling LLM behaviour remains unreliable, and experts cannot yet interpret what happens inside them (Eight Things).
Specific important capabilities can emerge unpredictably as models are scaled up (Eight Things).

recommendations.text: Build methods for scalable oversight so humans can supervise AI on tasks they can't check alone.
More NLP/ML researchers should engage with longer-term AI safety concerns.
